## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Maṇḍapeyyakathā* ("Discussion of 'A Fine Extract to be Drunk'") is the tenth chapter of the first major division (*Mahāvagga*) of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* [SuttaCentral; Buswell 2004]. In this discourse, the thirty-seven aids to awakening (the seven sets) alongside the four noble truths are singled out as the "fine extract" or "distilled essence" (*maṇḍapeyya*) of the teaching (*desanā*), indicating that the compiler of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* understood these core doctrinal sets to represent the essential core of the Buddha's dispensation [Gethin 2001].
DharmaNexus identifies extensive internal text reuse across the Pali Canon (435 matches shared with 46 other texts) [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments appear in other treatises of the *Paṭisambhidāmagga*, notably the *Virāgakathā* (Ps 2.5), *Ñāṇakathā* (Ps 1.1), *Bojjhaṅgakathā* (Ps 2.3), *Dhammacakkakathā* (Ps 2.7), and *Indriyakathā* (Ps 1.4), as well as the *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), the Yamaka (*Paṇṇattivāraniddesa*), and multiple commentaries including the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā* and *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Sanskrit works such as the *Arthaviniścayasūtra* and Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta*, Tibetan translations including the *Abhidharmakośaṭīkopayikā* and the *Arthaviniścayaṭīkā*, and Chinese canonical texts such as the *Madhyama Āgama* and *Saṃyukta Āgama* [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records four modern translations of the text in four languages [SuttaCentral].
